mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes SLC 220d or 250d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM651 engine for the SLC 220d or 250d costs £3,200-£4,800 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,200 depending on complexity - diesel work requires specialist knowledge.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes SLC 220d or 250d?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign on the OM651 engine. The rear-mounted timing chain tensioner can lose pressure, allowing chain slack and guide wear. If ignored, it can lead to catastrophic engine failure.

mainEntity.name: What causes injector failure on a Mercedes SLC 220d or 250d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Early OM651 engines used Delphi piezo injectors which developed a reputation for rough idle, limp mode, and high-pressure rail faults. These injectors are sensitive to fuel quality and operating conditions.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes SLC 220d or 250d engine (OM651) reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM651 is fundamentally reliable - 200,000-300,000 km examples are common. However, it has predictable weak points: timing chain stretch from approximately 120,000 km, injector failures, EGR clogging, and DPF issues. All are manageable with the right maintenance schedule.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes SLC 220d and 250d engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM651 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. Timing chain issues typically appear between 75,000-120,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes SLC 220d or 250d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the SLC is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt OM651 costs £3,200-£4,800 - far less than replacing a £12,000-£25,000 vehicle. SLC values remain strong for well-maintained examples, making engine replacement a worthwhile investment.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz SLC 220d/250d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The SLC 220d and SLC 250d launched with the R172 facelift in 2016 as the diesel options in the SLC range, powered by the OM651 2.1-litre twin-turbo four-cylinder diesel - a refined, torquey unit that offered excellent fuel economy and relaxed cruising. The SLC 250d produced 204hp and 500Nm of torque, making it the most powerful diesel SLC ever offered. Production continued until 2020 when the SLC was discontinued, making these models the final chapter of Mercedes' compact roadster lineage.

milestones.description: OM651.921, 2.1L twin-turbo diesel, 170hp @ 4,200rpm (SLC 220d, R172 facelift launch)
OM651.921 / OM651.980, 2.1L twin-turbo diesel, 204hp @ 4,200rpm, 500Nm @ 1,600rpm (SLC 250d, R172 facelift launch)
2020 - Both engines continue with 9G-TRONIC automatic transmission
End of SLC production; R172 platform retired

items.commonFailure: Timing chain stretch and guide wear - the OM651's single most critical failure point. The timing chain drives both camshafts and the high-pressure fuel pump. If it stretches beyond tolerance or a guide fails, the consequences range from misfires and cam/crank correlation codes to catastrophic engine damage if the chain jumps a tooth. Typical failure mileage: 75,000-120,000 miles (120,000-200,000 km). EGR valve clogging and injector failures are also common.

problems.group: OM651 Timing Chain Stretch & Guide Wear
problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Stretch & Guide Wear - The Most Critical Diesel Failure
problems.rootCause: The OM651's timing chain drives both camshafts and the high-pressure fuel pump. A hydraulic tensioner can lose pressure prematurely, allowing chain stretch and guide wear. If the chain jumps a tooth, the consequences range from misfires and cam/crank correlation codes to catastrophic engine damage. Cold-start rattling is the classic warning sign.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Timing chain inspection, camshaft correlation check, oil pressure test
repairOptions.longevity: First step - confirms whether chain or tensioner is the issue

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, guides, tensioner, inspect oil pump chain
repairOptions.longevity: If caught before chain stretch is severe

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine swap with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If timing failure has caused valve damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2016-2020 SLC 220d or 250d is worth approximately £12,000-£25,000 depending on mileage and condition. These premium roadsters retain strong values for well-maintained examples, making engine replacement a justifiable investment.
problems.recommendation: If your SLC 220d or 250d exhibits a rattling noise on cold start, act immediately. The OM651's timing chain is a known critical weakness. Specialist timing chain replacement at £1,600-£2,400 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates. If the chain has jumped timing, a full rebuilt OM651 engine with upgraded tensioner components is the only safe option.

problems.h4: OM651 Injector & EGR System Failure - Emissions and Driveability Issues
problems.rootCause: Early OM651 engines used Delphi piezo injectors which developed a reputation for rough idle, limp mode, and high-pressure rail faults. EGR valve clogging is also common, causing hesitation and reduced performance. DPF regeneration issues have been reported on vehicles used primarily for short urban journeys.

repairOptions.longevity: If caught early with mild symptoms

repairOptions.longevity: If injector or EGR failure has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: EGR and injector issues on the OM651 are common but often manageable. If you experience rough idle or limp mode, have the injectors tested immediately. Replacing a single faulty injector at a specialist (£400-£800) is cost-effective. However, if multiple injectors are failing, replacing all four with updated units is the smarter long-term investment.

problems.h4: OM651 DPF Regeneration & Emissions System Faults
problems.rootCause: DPF regeneration issues are common on vehicles used primarily for short urban journeys. The DPF requires sustained motorway speeds to reach regeneration temperature - if the car only reaches just above 300°C, regeneration fails and warning lights appear.

problems.recommendation: DPF issues on the OM651 are often a symptom of driving patterns rather than engine failure. Regular motorway driving helps keep the DPF clear. If you experience DPF warnings, a forced regeneration at £150-£300 is a cost-effective first step. If the DPF is blocked beyond regeneration, specialist replacement at £800-£1,600 is significantly cheaper than dealer rates.
